GameEventAction.Description:
A very long time ago, we Atuuk lived here on our world and only had each other for company. We didn't know we were lonely, because we didn't know there were nice aliens out there. Then came the Long-Ago Friends, who sent us the Big Gift: spaceships and computers and all kinds of interesting, mysterious things, and they all fell from the sky! It took us many years to reverse engineer the gifts of the Long-Ago Friends. Sometimes we understood these gifts quickly. Other times a few fires and explosions taught us that we had to rethink our assumptions.
Why did the Long-Ago Friends choose to greet us by sending their ships hurling to the ground in balls of flame? No one knows for sure, but our greatest minds believe that they wanted the Atuuk to experience the satisfaction of solving complex puzzles, such as how to make a broken ship fly.
And figure it out is exactly what we did! We studied and took apart the gifts from the Long-Ago Friends. The machines were complicated, and maybe we didn't always get everything exactly right, but we understood enough to reach the stars. We had one great mission: to find the Long-Ago Friends and thank them for the Big Gift.
But then there was a terrible war. Some aliens, who were not friendly, hurt a lot of people and destroyed many worlds. They broke space itself, which is hard to do and also embarrassing. We Atuuk, who had only just begun our journey to the stars, suffered a bit of a setback.
Finally, after many hundreds of years dedicated to problem-solving and big-thinking, we have returned to where we were before the Cataclysm. We are ready to visit the stars, and we are ready to resume our search for the Long-Ago Friends.
Who were they? Why did they give us the Big Gift of exploding ships and smashed computers? So many mysteries await, but we will find all the answers. We will learn who the Long-Ago Friends are, and we will visit them, and we will give them a long overdue hug.
Friendship awaits!

This is a delightful surprise! Here in our system, so close to our own home, we've found ruins. Someone built something on this world a long time ago. There might be interesting things here. We should take a look!

This is unexpected. We've poked around the ruins and found that some of the structures here resemble the technology given to us by the Long-Ago Friends. That's good!
Unfortunately, the Long-Ago Friends must have been concerned about bad people doing bad things, because the ruins are heavily mined. That's bad!

We could dedicate our best minds, who are very smart, to studying the outpost and finding a way to avoid the mines. We don't want to be blown up, but this kind of deep thinking can be expensive.
Or we could just blow up the ruins ourselves and see what resources we might find.
Space travel involves a lot of difficult choices. No one warned us about that.
GameEventAction.ChoiceButtonText: Pay to Fund a Lot of Thinking [-20,000cr]

GameEventAction.Description: Smart people have been thinking smart thoughts, and they've found a way to deactivate the mines. Let the exploring begin!

Now we know! The machines we've found here leave no doubt. This outpost was built by the Long-Ago Friends, though it has been so badly damaged over the years that it's difficult to guess what they were doing here.
We did find some weapons, and the mines surrounding the outpost suggest that they were worried about bad people stealing their things. Were there also Long-Ago enemies? Let's hope not.
Our scientists have been busy studying the artifacts the Long-Ago friends left behind, including some ships designed by our own ancestors. It's very flattering that the Long-Ago friends were so interested in the things we made from their gifts!
We also found a data crystal with a star map. It points to a [LOCATION]nearby location[/LOCATION], which might be worth investigating.
Unfortunately, our scientists are now very tired from all their research. They are going to need to rest before they're ready to get back to work.
Our new Escorts are called [HL]Wonderfully Eventful Vacation[/HL] and [HL]My Second Favorite Uncle[/HL].

There were probably some interesting things in those ruins. It looks like we'll never know! There's no point in worrying about what you can't change. Besides, we found some useful items once the mines finished exploding.
One of the few things we found intact was a data crystal with a star map. It points to a nearby location, which might be worth investigating. Maybe whatever is at that location is also surrounded by mines, and we can blow that up too!
We have recieved:
1000 Polymer 1000 Nekros Stone 1000 Silicon

The ancient Atuuk were everywhere it seems!
Here on this world we've found the ruins of a facility we believe was used by the intrepid Atuuk of the old galaxy. Many of the structures have been destroyed, but we hope to learn more about what our people were doing here. It was probably something very interesting.

GameEventAction.MessageTitle: Dead People who did Great Things
GameEventAction.Description:
On this world we've found a tomb dedicated to many of the important Atuuk leaders of the time before the great Cataclysm: Ibif, an extra smart scientist. Kulupi, a persuasive diplomat, Humlipo, a skilled general, and many others.
Truly, our ancestors possessed some amazing abilities.

GameEventAction.GeneratedItemName: The Tomb of Some Very Smart People 3 (Atuuk)

GameEvent.Name: The Tomb of Some Very Smart People 3 (Atuuk)

GameEventAction.Description:
All across our civilization, the Atuuk are inspired by the deeds of our ancestors. The people want to be like these great Atuuk, who always pursued a Great Direction, a single goal that became the focus of all Atuuk society. Nothing makes us happier than working together as a united people, all pursuing greatness in a single discipline.
Changing our Great Direction may lead to reduced interest in our previous obsession, but that's the price you pay for being super-excited about something. We're not obsessive. We're locked in!
Now we must decide. In the cities, in the markets, on the streets, we speak to one another in shouts and whispers, and a consensus rises to the surface. Will our people keep our current Great Direction or choose a new one?
GameEventAction.ImageFilepath: Environment/Events/the tomb of some very smart people

GameEventAction.Description: We have a new Great Direction! Look out, galaxy, the Atuuk are inspired to do amazing things!
Continuing on the way we've been going is best. Never look back! That's the Atuuk way!

Within the Tomb we have also discovered an ancient machine that creates a small figurine of all the heroes honored here. There is only enough material to make one last statue, and our exploration team huddled around the device to watch the plastic poured into the two halves of the mold, which were then pressed together. As they watched in amazement, the completed statuette dropped down into a slot from which they retrieved it. What wonders our ancestors created.
The figurine is hollow within and made of surprisingly light plastic. Some might call this memento cheap looking. There are visible seams where the two halves were joined together, but who cares? The Figurine of Inspiring Heroes makes us happy, and we have no doubt our people will flock from all over to look at it.

GameEvent.Name: Investigate The Long-Ago Friends Research Center 2 (Atuuk)

GameEventAction.Description:
We've explored the ruins on this world and found a research center dedicated to finding the Long-Ago Friends, who helped our ancestors reach the stars.
Whatever our ancestors discovered has been lost, unfortunately. It appears that the research center was raided in the war before the Cataclysm. In fact, the skeletal remains of ancient Atuuk can be found everywhere. It looks like some extremely unkind people attacked the research center and did mean and violent things.
This is upsetting. But maybe it's not as bad as it seems. Maybe there was an accident or a space virus that turned reasonable people into killers. Or mass insanity. Anything is possible. Right now, we just don't know, and not knowing might be the best thing.
If the people back home were to learn of a massacre against the Atuuk, even an ancient one, it could prove very upsetting. On the other hand, knowing things also has value.

A careful examination of the outpost has helped us put together a rough idea of what happened here.
Aliens arrived at this research facility and our ancestors, in their enthusiasm, must have assumed they were the Long-Ago Friends. This was a big mistake because not everyone is as friendly as the real Friends. These aliens were definitely not friendly.

Why were they interested in Atuuk brains? It is very flattering, of course, that they wanted to understand how we achieved so much, but they could have simply asked. Maybe the raiders eventually realized that and then felt terrible about their bad behavior. We've searched for evidence of an apology, but have not found one.
This has all proved to be very troubling. As we feared, the people back home don't like the idea of Long-Ago Enemies or brain-obsessed raiders. Even so, our careful examination of the wreckage has advanced our knowledge, which proves that there is good to be found in even the worst situations.

We've done a quick survey of the research center, but we haven't asked any hard questions. It's better that way.
The people back home seem very appreciative that we are not spending our time learning things it's better not to know.

Skeletal remains of ancient Atuuk can be found everywhere. Evidence suggests that the research center was attacked, though we can assume little else without further study.

GameEventAction.GeneratedItemName: Leave the Research Center Choice (Non Atuuk)

GameEventAction.Description:
A careful examination of the research center has helped us put together a rough idea of what happened here.
Aliens arrived at this research facility and the Attuk likely mistook them for the benevolent aliens they sought. This was, for them, a terrible error.

Many Atuuk were killed and captured. In addition to fragments of weapons, we found scientific instruments in the research center. These belonged to the raiders and appear to be designed to measure Atuuk brains. This seems like a curious task, and we cannot conclude what the belligerent aliens were after.
We've discovered a world that appears to be populated by Atuuk. It's always nice to make new friends! We've sent them a message, and we look forward to hearing their reply.

We're receiving a message from the Atuuk world.
"We cautiously acknowledge you, strangers. We are also confused, because we have not heard from any other Atuuk for many centuries. Why should that be? If there had been any sort of galactic crisis that would prevent communication, we'd have known about it. We are too smart to miss something like that. We can only conclude we are being shunned.
We have long wondered why other Atuuk would be so mean to us, and we've realized that the only answer is jealousy. You are jealous that we are so much smarter than other Atuuk. And now you come to us, probably because you want something. We don't have much here, but we have our pride. And our intelligence! We'll listen to what you have to say, but don't expect us to do you any big favors. We are still mad."

These Atuuk are strange. And confused. They clearly know nothing about the ancient war and the great Cataclysm. This must have been a small colony that found itself isolated after the war and never understood the reason for that isolation.
We have attempted to communicate with them and explain how they were separated from the rest of the Atuuk, but they don't believe us. They claim they are too smart to be fooled by our lies.
This is all very sad because their world is struggling, and they could benefit from our help. With our guidance, there's no reason why their world couldn't thrive. But how to convince them to cooperate.

Our smartest people think there are two options. We could bribe them, which would be expensive, but is sure to work. Alternatively, we could attempt to impress them with our superior intelligence, which would make them understand they should defer to us. Our most experienced diplomats think this might work, but there are no guarantees. Space decisions are challenging.

Everyone likes money! A few credits in the right hands, and now we're all friends. We should continue to work to improve our relations with these Atuuk. Their very pleasant world would thrive under our impressive leadership.
We like money!

GameEventAction.MessageTitle: We Showed Them Who Is Smart
GameEventAction.Description:
These people are very pleased with themselves, but, like all Atuuk, they are both curious and rational. We presented them with a lovingly made FOUR-COLOR brochure explaining not only the ancient war and the Cataclysm, but how we, the truly smart Atuuk, labored diligently to make our way back to space. Once copies of our brochure began to spread, Atuuk all over their world began to agree that they'd misjudge us. Now they've all come together, speaking with one voice about how impressive and likable we are.
We should continue to work to improve our relations with these Atuuk. Their world would thrive under our impressive leadership.
We're Impressed!

There is an old Atuuk saying: Stupid people are too stupid to know how stupid they are. The wisdom of the ancients has been proven. We put together a special brochure depicting our many successes, but they did not believe us. They said brochures could be faked. Who would make a fake brochure? It wouldn't even be a brochure anymore, it would be a story! We tried to explain this, but they would not listen. These Atuuk are stubborn as well as stupid. We have declared them the worst Atuuk ever, though we did not tell them that. It would hurt their feelings.
Now they dislike us, which is too bad. Their world is backwards and would do much better under our leadership. We should continue to work to find ways to improve their opinion of us and maybe, someday, we could show them a better way.
We dislike insults!

We've located the wreck of an ancient ship that crashed on the surface of this world. The remains of the ship are strewn along a crumbling precipice. Very dramatic. Our Atuuk-remains-detection machine is flashing aggressively. Unless it's malfunctioning (again!), there are probably some Atuuk remains on this world we've encountered. We should survey it further to see what's going on.

GameEventAction.MessageTitle: It's Hard not to be Cynical Sometimes
GameEventAction.Description:
Far beneath the surface of this world, we found an ancient prison from before the Cataclysm. It looks like Atuuk were held and subjected to experiences that were not very nice. Maybe even torture. A quick examination has already given us reason to think that these Atuuk were being held by another, presumably very mean, species.
Who would capture and imprison Atuuk, and for what reason? The galaxy is full of a lot of great people, but when you find something like this and it can ruin your faith in others.
Back home, there is already a growing "Forget the Prison" movement. As the old Atuuk saying goes, "If you can't see it, then it probably doesn't exist." Many Atuuk are determined not to learn difficult truths.
Yet there are those who espouse radical beliefs and shout, "Knowing is good!" We have a tough decision to make.

As suspected, there are a bunch more ancient Atuuk corpses in the prison, but this happened a long time ago. The mean people aren't around anymore. Even so, the place was very spooky. Our explorers grabbed a few data crystals, which looked like they held technical specs, and got the heck out of there. There's no point in looking back.

The goings-on at this prison were quite strange and hard to piece together. Hundreds of Atuuk were held here, but we couldn't find any records of them having been charged with crimes. They seem to have been brought here by another species, which is odd.
There are some deeply troubling images in the archives showing ships that might have belonged to Long-Ago Friends. We haven't found any evidence that they were held prisoner on this world too, and we certainly hope they weren't. They deserve better. Still, if we could find some of their remains, it might help us locate them and thank them for the Big Gift.

The prison appears to have been overseen by the bad guys of the old Galaxy, the Shakturi, which is very scary. Translating the records that remain is a challenge, but based on some documentation we found in a non-Shakturi language, the Atuuk were being examined regarding something called a "Psychic nullification field." None of our scientists have ever heard of this before, and they are assuming it's something the Shakturi made up in order to sound impressive. Regardless, the people back home have been very distressed to learn about the Shakturi treatment of the Atuuk. Yes, it was a long time ago, but that sort of cruelty is always upsetting.
Otherwise, we found some data crystals with technical specifications for our people to review. There was also a star map with a location marked. Anything could be there. We should go!

Far beneath the surface of this world, we found an ancient prison from before the Cataclysm. It appears that aliens were held here and interrogated by members of another species. If we wish to explore further, we may learn more.

A cursory examination has revealed that aliens of one species, the Atuuk, were held here by members of another species we could not identify.
Most of the files are garbled or unintelligible, but we have obtained some schematics that might help us with our research.

A thorough examination has revealed that aliens of one species, the Atuuk, were held here by the Shakturi. Translating the records that remain is a challenge, but documentation we found in a non-Shakturi language mention something called a "Psychic nullification field."
We also found some data crystals with technical specifications for our people to review. There was also a star map with a location marked.
The defenses have been destroyed and we can now explore the planet's surface.

The fortifications surrounding this world are scary, but they are clearly designed by the Long-Ago Friends. There is no sign of life below, and the defenses are ancient, dating back to before the Cataclysm, so it seems unlikely the Long-Ago Friends would mind if we destroyed their security systems. In fact, they would probably want us to.
We have dedicated so much of our brain-power to studying the Long-Ago Friends' technology that we might be able to find a way to remotely deactivate at least some of the defences. Alternatively, we could use our military might and prove to the galaxy that the Atuuk are strong as well as smart.

GameEventAction.Description: This world is protected by ancient defenses. We can dedicate our resources to shutting down some of the automated systems, though doing so will be expensive. Or we could simply attack.
GameEventAction.GeneratedItemName: Invest in Shutting Down Defenses Choice (Non Atuuk)

GameEvent.Name: Invest in Shutting Down Defenses Choice (Non Atuuk)

GameEventAction.Description:
Using our analysis machines and investigation tools, we've confirmed that these bases were indeed built by the Long-Ago Friends. That they gave us the Big Gift proves they were nice, so they must have been fighting some very wicked people to make such strong defenses. But those bad people are out of the way now.
It's time to start looking through their things!

So much of the base has been destroyed. It is impossible to know what the Long-Ago Friends looked like or what they were doing here.
We did find some medical files about Atuuk anatomy, specifically Atuuk brains. It is very touching how much they thought about us. Maybe they were planning to give the Atuuk another Big Gift. Whatever bad guys they were fighting probably made that impossible. War is terrible.

But there is good news. In the base's wreckage we found a data crystal with a map to a world that we believe might have been a colony of the Long-Ago Friends! Yes, we should finally be able to visit them and thank them for the Big Gift. We are trying not to get our hopes up, because we know this map is very old, and the galaxy has gone through some changes since it was made, but it's hard to contain our excitement. Maybe they even know we are coming and are planning to have a party for us. It's not unreasonable. One thing we know for sure: reuniting with the Long-Ago Friends is going to be a great time!
[ARTIFACT]We also found a recording containing music that many of our soldiers find extremely inspiring[/ARTIFACT]. We have already decided that troops should listen to this whenever they go into battle. Our linguistics experts have translated some of the lyrics, and they are weirdly aggressive, as though soldiers should be happy about going into battle. It's strange that the Friends would write a song like this, but sometimes enthusiasm is what you need to win. Listening to this music should make our soldiers even stronger and more courageous than they already are.

Much of the base has been destroyed. It is impossible to know what civilization built this fortress or for what purpose. However, it appears that some portion, perhaps a large portion, of the base's personnel were engaged in a project investigating certain cognitive powers of the Atuuk.

[ARTIFACT]We also found a recording or martial music that our soldiers find strangely affecting[/ARTIFACT]. The effect appears to transcend species, and our preliminary studies suggest listening to this music will make soldier more courageous and effective.
We have also found a star map with [LOCATION]a location identified[/LOCATION], though we do not know what we will find there.

GameEvent.Name: The Return of the Long-Ago Friends (Atuuk)

GameEventAction.Description: We have found the home of the Long-Ago Friends! It appears to be uninhabited and in ruins. Many terrible things happened during the ancient war, so we can only hope the Friends were able to relocate to a safe place. Once we survey the planet, we will know more!

This world was once Boskara. Important for alliance with Shakturi in ancient times. In those days, before the Cataclysm, Boskara used this world to study Atuuk and to transport them to separate Shakturi base. Shakturi showed much interest in Atuuk, who were immune to psychic warfare.

This world once belonged to the Boskara, who were in league with the Shakturi. In the days before the Cataclysm, this world was dedicated to studying the Atuuk and to transporting them to a separate Shakturi base. The Shakturi appear to have particularly interested in the Atuuk immunity to psychic warfare.

Now that we have reached the surface, there have been some... disappointing revelations. In the years before the Cataclysm, this world belonged to the Boskara, and they were not friends at all. They were mean!
This world was a Boskara outpost, used as a place to house captured Atuuk. These Atuuk prisoners were studied and experimented on. It was a place where very unkind acts were committed.

The Boskara were in league with the Shakturi, who for some reason seemed very interested in the Atuuk and how our minds work. According to records, thousands of Atuuk were to be transported to the Shakturi, which sounds like a very bad thing. Maybe they admired us for our focus and determination, but they seem to have been particularly concerned that of all the species in the galaxy, only the Atuuk are immune to Shakturi psychic warfare. That's how good the Atuuk are.
It is clear that the Shakturi wanted to understand how the Atuuk could be so resistant to their weapons, so they sent the Boskara to our world to do bad things. Then the Boskara were attacked by a group of aliens called the Freedom Alliance. Fleets belonging to the Ackdarians, Humans, Ikkuro, and Zenox destroyed the Boskara invaders, causing many of their ships to fall to our world.
The Boskara did not intend for their ships and machines to be a Big Gift. They meant to hurt and imprison us! It was the Freedom Alliance that gave us a Big Gift, even if they never intended to.

Our careful examination of the records has taught us a great deal about the Boskara. They did terrible things a long time ago. Maybe they've changed for the better, but it would be wise to be careful before rushing into any agreements with them. Maybe with anyone. The galaxy is a dangerous place.
We've been combing through the remaining structures on this world, looking to see what we can learn from and reverse engineer. The Boskara were not nice, but they were smart!
We've also found an interesting device called the [ARTIFACT]Tactical Bombardment Computer[/ARTIFACT], which can help us launch assaults on alien worlds. Let's hope we never need to use it!
These have been some troubling revelations, but we've learned a great deal, and we are now ready to face our future with new friends and technology. This is a good day for the Atuuk!
We Know You Aren't Real Friends!

Records suggest that during the ancient war, the Boskara attacked the Atuuk homeworld on behalf of Shakturi. During the attack, the Boskara fleet became the victim of a treacherous sneak attack by a coalition of Ackdarians, Humans, Ikkuro, and Zenox. Through cowardly means, they destroyed Boskara fleet. Many ships crashed on the Atuuk world.
The Atuuk were able to reverse engineer the Boskara technology. The Atuuk reached the stars on the backs of the Boskara.
We have found a device called the [ARTIFACT]Tactical Bombardment Computer[/ARTIFACT], which augments the bombardment of a planet. We will make good use of this.

Records suggest that during the ancient war, the Boskara attacked the Atuuk homeworld on behalf of the Shakturi. During the attack, the Boskara fleet was surprised by a coalition of Ackdarians, Humans, Ikkuro, and Zenox. They destroyed the Boskara fleet, and several ships crashed on the Atuuk world.
The Atuuk were able to reverse engineer the Boskara technology in a surprisingly short period of time. That is how the Atuuk reached the stars.
We have also found a device called the [ARTIFACT]Tactical Bombardment Computer[/ARTIFACT], which appears to augment the bombardment of a planet.
There's some kind of interesting structure on this world. We should survey it and find out more!

The Boskara used this world to develop their weapons technology and plan their conquests. They seem to have been weirdly dedicated to taking other people's stuff by force.
Once we thought the aliens who sent us the Big Gift had to be the kindest, most generous beings in the galaxy. We've had a rude awakening, and we must be careful not to be let terrible things happen to us the way our ancestors were hurt by the Boskara.
This Weapons Academy will help us protect ourselves, control our own future, and push back when the dangerous forces of the galaxy attempt to bully us. We can hope to never need it, but there is a lot of danger out there, and we Atuuk can't let ourselves be fooled again.
There is an interesting structure on the world below. We should further survey it to learn more.
The ancient Boskara used this world to develop their weapons. We can do so again.

GameEventAction.Description:
